questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 7]

Janie claims Australian rabbits have longer ears than Spanish rabbits. Random samples were measured to the nearest millimetre. Australia has median 80 mm and interquartile range 11 mm.

[Box-and-whisker diagram for Spain on a 44–92 mm scale: minimum 46, Q₁=68, median 75, Q₃=84, maximum 89.]

(a) Complete the table.

[Table: columns Australia, Spain; Median (mm): 80, blank; Interquartile range (mm): 11, blank.] [3]

(b) Justifying your answers, compare the distributions using (i) the median; (ii) the interquartile range. [4]
questions.solution: (a) Spain’s median is 75 mm and IQR=84−68=16 mm. (b)(i) Australia’s median 80>75, suggesting Australian rabbits generally have longer ears. (ii) Spain’s IQR 16>11, so the middle 50% of Spanish ear lengths is more variable.

2. [Maximum mark: 7]

Darren buys a car for $35 000. Its value decreases by 15% in the first year.

(a) Find its value after the first year. [2]

After the first year, it decreases by 11% each subsequent year.

(b) Find its value 10 years after purchase, to the nearest dollar. [2]

After n complete years its value is less than 10% of the original.

(c) Find the least n. [3]

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

A right cone monument has vertical height 20 m. Oliver stands 5 m from its base. His eye is 1.8 m above ground and the angle of elevation to the vertex is 58°.

[Diagram, not to scale: cone of height 20 m; Oliver is 5 m beyond the rim, eye height 1.8 m; line of sight to vertex makes 58° with horizontal.]

(a) Find the base radius. [3]

(b) Find the monument’s volume. [2]
questions.summary: Use right-triangle trigonometry and cone volume.
questions.solution: (a) The vertical rise is 20−1.8=18.2 m and horizontal distance to the axis is r+5. Thus tan58°=18.2/(r+5), giving r=6.37262…≈6.37 m. (b) V=(1/3)πr²(20)=850.540…≈851 m³.

X is normally distributed with mean 10 and standard deviation 2.

(a) Find P(X is more than 1.5 standard deviations above the mean). [2]

P(X is more than k standard deviations above the mean)=0.1, k∈ℝ.

(b) Find k. [2]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

A particle passes O at t=0. For 0≤t≤10 its velocity is v=2sin(0.5t)+0.3t−2 m s⁻¹.

[Graph: velocity starts at −2, crosses zero near t=1.69, reaches a positive maximum, crosses again near t=6.12, then is negative to t=10.]

(a) Find the smallest t when it changes direction. [2]

(b) Find the range of t for which displacement is increasing. [2]

(c) Find displacement relative to O at t=10. [2]
questions.solution: (a) Solving v=0 gives first root t=1.68694…≈1.69 s. (b) Displacement increases when v>0: 1.69<t<6.12. (c) ∫₀¹⁰[2sin(0.5t)+0.3t−2]dt=−2.13464…≈−2.13 m.

6. [Maximum mark: 7]

Ten students’ Test A and Test B scores are:

[Table: Student 1–10. Test A: 52,71,100,93,81,80,88,100,70,61. Test B: 58,80,92,98,90,82,100,100,65,74.]

Let x be Test A and y Test B. The regression line of y on x is y=0.822x+18.4.

(a) Find Pearson’s r. [2]

Paulo scored 10 on Test A; y=0.822(10)+18.4≈27 was used to estimate Test B.

(b) Give a reason this is inappropriate. [1]

Giovanni scored 90 on Test B; solving 90=0.822x+18.4 gave x≈87.

(c) (i) Give a reason this is inappropriate. (ii) Use an appropriate method to show the estimated Test A score is 86 to the nearest integer. [4]
questions.solution: (a) Calculator regression gives r=0.901017…≈0.901. (b) x=10 is far outside the observed Test A range 52–100, so this is extrapolation. (c)(i) A y-on-x line must not be inverted to predict x from y. (ii) The x-on-y regression is x=0.987124y−3.21970; at y=90, x=85.6214…≈86.

7. [Maximum mark: 12]

Let f(x)=(3/2)e^(x−2), 0≤x≤4.

(a) Show f⁻¹(x)=2+ln(2x/3). [3]

The graphs of f and f⁻¹ intersect at P and Q.

[Diagram: increasing exponential f and concave-down logarithmic f⁻¹ intersect twice on y=x at P and Q.]

(b) Find PQ. [3]

Reflect f in the x-axis, then translate 5 units upward to form g.

(c) Write down (i) g(x); (ii) the domain of g. [3]

(d) Solve f(x)=g(x), in the form x=a+ln b, a,b∈ℚ. [3]
questions.summary: Work with an exponential inverse and transformations.

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

At Sule Skerry, water height is H(t)=1.63sin(0.513(t−8.20))+2.13 metres, t hours after midnight.

[Graph for 0≤t≤15 showing one low and one high tide; low height 0.50 m, high 3.76 m.]

(a) The first low-to-high interval is 6 hours m minutes. Find m to nearest integer. [3]

(b) Between consecutive high tides, find how long H<1 m. [2]

(c) Find the rate of change at t=13, in m/h. [2]

At Rockall, h(t)=a sin(b(t−c))+d, a,b,c,d>0. First low tide is 02:41 at 0.40 m; first high tide is 09:02 at 2.74 m.

(d) Find a,b,c,d. [7]

(e) Find the first T when the two heights are equal. [2]
questions.summary: Analyze and compare sinusoidal tide models.

9. [Maximum mark: 16]

All angles are in degrees. A wall OA is 50 m long. A hedge meets it at O at 28°. A 25 m fence AB runs from A to point B on the hedge, forming triangular field OAB.

[Diagram, not to scale: OA along wall, OB along hedge at 28° to OA, AB=25 m and OA=50 m.]

(a) (i) Find the two possible sizes of OÂB. (ii) Hence find the two possible areas of OAB. [8]

A second fence CD of length 10 m forms smaller triangle OCD inside OAB, with C on wall, D on hedge, and area 60 m². Let x=OC and y=OD.

[Diagram: triangle OCD at O inside OAB; ∠COD=28°, CD=10 m.]

(b) Show x²+y²=100+240/tan28°. [5]

(c) Hence determine the two possible lengths of OC. [3]
questions.summary: Solve ambiguous triangles and a constrained inner triangle.
questions.solution: (a) By sine rule, sin B/50=sin28°/25, so B=69.8748° or 110.125°. Hence A=82.1251° or 41.8748°, i.e. 82.1° or 41.9°. Areas are (1/2)(50)(25)sin A=619 m² or 417 m². (b) Cosine rule: 100=x²+y²−2xy cos28°. Area gives (1/2)xy sin28°=60, so xy=120/sin28°. Substitute to obtain x²+y²=100+240/tan28°. (c) Solving with xy fixed gives x=13.1300… or 19.4673…, so OC=13.1 m or 19.5 m.
